title: KV tile serializer + FlashAttention integration (draft)
content:
Purpose

Sketch for a compact, tile-oriented serializer for paged KV that integrates cleanly with FlashAttention kernels and reduces host<->device transfer overhead. This doc collects design ideas, performance tradeoffs, and a rough prototype plan for a serializer+unpack kernel that: 

- stores KV in compact on-disk / in-heap tiles (delta/quantized)
- streams and decompresses tiles into GPU memory in a FlashAttention-friendly layout
- minimizes copies and synchronization across streams
- provides a graceful fallback for cold misses and high-concurrency bursts

Context / motivation

Current paged-KV approach: each request may trigger small, sparse page reads, then tensor reshapes and KV assembly on GPU. We see latency and throughput overhead from:

1. many small device allocations / cudaMemcpy calls
2. layout conversions (N, H, E) -> FlashAttention QKV layout
3. per-request padding and alignment waste for odd sequence lengths
4. CPU-side unpacking and reserialize for GPU kernel consumption

Aim: push as much of the layout work into a single, vectorized device-side "unpack-and-place" kernel so the host only streams compact tiles and a small placement descriptor. This reduces PCIe/DRAM bandwidth and number of sync points.

Key idea: KV tile serializer format

Tile structure (compact):
- header (8B): tile_id, compressed_size, flags
- metadata (variable): per-shard quantization meta, scale/zero-point for per-row quant, tile shape (T tokens x D dim)
- payload: packed bytes. Payload encoding options: 16-bit float (FP16), 8-bit dynamic quant (int8 + per-row scale), or run-length deltas (for sparse KV).

On-disk / in-heap layout is row-major within a token tile. But the device wants a layout interleaved by head for FlashAttention (H, T, Dh). The serializer records original (T, D) and an instruction descriptor for the unpack kernel: how to map contiguous tile bytes to the output KV buffer (base pointer + stride + element size).

Unpack kernel responsibilities

- decompress/convert payload to target element type (FP16 / BF16 / TF32 path)
- write elements to pre-allocated device KV slab using vectorized stores (float4/short2) with coalesced patterns
- perform head-wise transposition when needed (token-major -> head-major) using shared memory for tiles that fit SM scratch
- apply per-row scale/zero point if quantized
- optionally perform lightweight fusion: if the request arrives with immediate FlashAttention call, the unpack kernel can precompute and place KV in the exact FlashAttention tensors (no further transposes)

API between prefetcher and serving runtime

Host prefetcher:
- issues async read of tile (from local cache or S3) into pinned host staging buffer
- constructs a tiny descriptor (tile_id, dst_gpu_slab_base, token_offset, flags, shape, quant_meta)
- invokes cudaMemcpyAsync to device-staging buffer followed by a cudaLaunch of unpack kernel on a dedicated stream assigned to that request cohort

Serving runtime:
- maintains per-GPU "KV slab allocator": large pre-reserved device buffers with coarse-grained slots (tile-sized)
- request execution threads allocate target ranges and publish placement descriptors into a ring buffer consumed by unpack kernels

Kernel-level design notes

1) Streams and ordering
- Use 3 streams per GPU: io-stream (memcpyAsync H2D pinned->device staging), unpack-stream (kernel launches for unpack), compute-stream (FlashAttention invocation).
- Stream dependence: set compute-stream to wait on an event signaled by unpack-stream when target region is fully written. This preserves overlap: memcpyAsync can overlap with previous compute work; unpack kernel runs while compute works on other requests.

2) Shared memory transposition
- For tiles of size <= 512 tokens * Dh small (e.g., Dh <= 64), do shared-memory transpose to avoid strided global writes. Use 32x32 or 64x32 block transposes tuned to SM L1 limits.
- For larger tiles, do warp-level vectorized stores in chunks to keep coalescing and avoid overuse of shared memory.

3) Vectorized paths and alignment
- Serializer must pad payloads to 32B boundaries when possible so device memcpy + vector loads (float4) behave well. Add a small per-tile padding field in header.
- Unpack kernel should check alignment and select between unaligned byte-copy + conversion vs aligned vector loads. Avoid branching inside warps as much as possible.

4) Quantization interplay
- Provide three quant paths: per-row int8 + float32 scale, per-tile 4-bit group quant (similar to GPTQ-ish packed nibbles), and FP16 pass-through. Runtime chooses based on accuracy target and memory.
- The unpack kernel must support fused dequantize store (read int8, multiply by scale, store as FP16) in one pass to avoid extra temp buffers. Use tensorcore-friendly FP16 writes when target is FP16.

5) Fusion with FlashAttention
- FlashAttention expects Q,K,V in specific layouts. Add a step where final KV writes are placed into an "attention slab" that is pinned to be passed directly to the FlashAttention call. The unpack kernel can optionally write into the compute slab used by FlashAttention and call a lightweight barrier/event.
- For streaming attention where KV evolves incrementally (LM streaming), perform partial tile unpack (only new token rows) and append into the ring buffer without re-transposing entire slab.

Microbenchmarks to run (proto plan)

- baseline: naive host-decompress -> cudaMemcpy H2D -> host kernel transpose -> FlashAttention call (current baseline)
- proto-1: host-decompress -> cudaMemcpy pinned -> device unpack kernel -> FlashAttention (no shared memory transpose)
- proto-2: shared-memory transpose path for small tiles
- proto-3: int8 quant path with fused dequantize-store
- metrics: end-to-end P95 latency for single-request cold miss, throughput for mixed request sizes, device occupancy, extra DRAM bandwidth, measured PCIe traffic

Expected tradeoffs / failure modes

- If unpack kernel uses too much shared memory per block, occupancy will drop; need auto-tuning thresholds (tile size -> path selection)
- Many small tile misses at high concurrency could create kernel launch saturation. Mitigation: batch unpack descriptors in the ring buffer and run a single kernel that processes multiple tiles (cohorting).
- Quant-decompress costs on GPU vs memory savings: for very small tiles quantization may not pay off (convert cost > bandwidth save). Use heuristics: if tile_size * concurrency > threshold then use quant.

Proto implementation plan (milestones)

1. Minimal unpack kernel (no transpose, FP16 only) + host-side serializer (fast path). Measure latency. (2 weeks)
2. Add pinned staging + stream separation + event sync. Run basic concurrency bench. (1 week)
3. Implement shared-memory transpose path + autotuner for tile size -> path. (2 weeks)
4. Add int8 dequantize fusion + per-row scales + fallback logic. (2 weeks)
5. Integrate with FlashAttention call path: event-based handoff and run end-to-end tests with Streaming LM and chat workloads. (2 weeks)
6. Add operator-level tests, accuracy checks (against FP32 baseline), and perf dashboards. (1 week)

Open questions / TODOs

- Exact header/descriptor compact encoding (should descriptor be 64B aligned?)
- Fallback compaction strategy for transient OOM on device slab allocation: evict oldest tiles vs per-request fallback to host transpose
- How to version serializer format safely across rolling upgrades (include format version in header)
- Evaluate hardware NVLink vs PCIe differences for multi-GPU shared slab approaches

Notes / references

- Related internal threads: slack #paged-kv (May 2024) for cache policy context
- See PR for async-prefetcher ring-buffer: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2381
- Jira ENG-1427: KV tile format proposals (linked above)

Appendix: rough kernel pseudocode

  int tile_idx = blockIdx.x;
  Descriptor d = desc[tile_idx];
  // compute local offsets, pointer into payload
  uint8_t *p = payload + d.payload_offset;
  // path selection: quantized vs fp16
  if (d.flags & FLAG_INT8) {
    // read 16 bytes at a time, dequantize to FP16 and write to kv_slab using vector stores
  } else {
    // direct cast copy into slab with optional transpose using shared memory for small tiles
  }
  // optionally write event or set atomic flag to signal completion for that tile's slab region
}

End.

Comments welcome — primarily tagging Alex/Diego/Priya for follow-ups. This is intended to be a lightweight, implementable sketch rather than a finished RFC.
